classification.reason: Request is a scientific goal or asks for planning without a concrete workflow.

assumptions: Unconditional de novo backbone generation is used; no binding target, functional hotspot, or topology constraint was provided.
Backbone length is set to 70–100 residues to favour a compact, likely soluble fold with manageable compute cost.

RFdiffusion top_candidates objects are assumed to expose a per-design sequence field; if absent at runtime the downstream ESM3 and protein_qc foreach nodes will not execute and rank_designs will aggregate structural metadata only.
ESM3 is run with sequence, structure, and embedding tracks to return joint foldability confidence and embeddings as prediction evidence for ranking.
A single design (num_designs: 1) keeps GPU use minimal; rank_designs top_k: 1 reflects the single-candidate scope.
No symmetry, partial diffusion, motif scaffolding, or binder-design constraints are applied; all scientific limitations of unconditional generation apply.
plan.goal: Generate one small (~70–100 aa) de novo soluble protein backbone with RFdiffusion, jointly evaluate its sequence and structure quality with ESM3, perform lightweight solubility QC (pLDDT, GRAVY, instability index, pI, polybasic patch), and return a ranked single-candidate output.

success_criteria.backbone_generated: rfdiffusion returns at least 1 design in top_candidates
success_criteria.esm3_quality: ESM3 confidence_scores and predicted_pdb returned for the candidate
success_criteria.qc_solubility: protein_qc metrics show GRAVY < 0 and instability_index < 40 and no polybasic flag
success_criteria.ranked_output: rank_designs returns ranked_candidates list with at least 1 entry and produces ranked_tsv artifact
